_comment: Shared validation fixtures for the TeamDef graph. ONE file, TWO validators.
consumer 1: src/lib/validate.test.ts — the canvas's TypeScript mirror.
consumer 2: loomcycle's internal/teamgraph shared-cases test, which reads
once the component is integrated there.
The canvas mirrors teamgraph.Validate so an operator sees a broken graph
while drawing rather than when op=create refuses it. Two implementations of
one rule set drift, silently, and this file is what stops it: a rule added
to validate.go without a case here is a rule the canvas will not surface.
Shipping the fixture in the package (package.json `files`) is what lets the
coupling survive the repo boundary instead of becoming a copy that rots.
go_valid / ts_valid are separate on purpose. They agree everywhere except
where RFC CZ decision 3 requires them not to — an unknown handler kind is an
error to the runtime and merely UNKNOWN to a canvas that may simply be older
than the runtime. Any case where they differ must say why in why_divergent.
NOTE: until the loomcycle integration lands, go_valid is an UNVERIFIED claim
about the Go validator. It was checked by hand against internal/teamgraph at
loomcycle 61de2cbb; the integration test is what makes it self-enforcing.

cases.why_divergent: RFC CZ decision 3. The runtime rejects a kind it does not implement, and must. The canvas must NOT: it may be an older build talking to a newer runtime, and refusing to render a `starter` would push the operator back to hand-editing JSON. The canvas renders it opaque, preserves it byte-for-byte, reports it at info, and lets the server be the authority.
